::: {.lead-large}
This is a colleagues-only field guide to a particular way of using LLMs:
**giving an AI agent direct access to your project files** so it can write
code, edit your LaTeX, audit a replication package, and run things on your
behalf — under your supervision.

It is *not* about chatting with ChatGPT in a browser. That is useful too,
but it isn't what's changed in the last year.
:::

## Who this is for

You are an economist who:

- Spends real hours writing Stata/R/Python/Matlab/Julia code, formatting
  LaTeX papers, building tables, or wrangling a replication package.
- Has heard "AI agents" get hyped and would like a non-marketing
  explanation of what's actually useful and what is not.
- Wants the **shortest possible path** from "I've heard of Claude Code"
  to "Claude Code is editing my paper while I review the diff."

You don't need to know git, the terminal, or any web technology beyond
the basics. We'll cover the parts that matter.

## What this guide is *not*

- **Not a sales pitch.** Claude Code is one tool in a busy landscape. The
  [comparison page](big-picture/landscape.qmd) explains where it fits next
  to Cursor, ChatGPT, and Copilot, and when each is the right call.
- **Not for confidential or restricted-access data.** If you work with
  IRB-protected, FERPA-covered, Census, IRS, or other restricted data,
  read the [confidential data page](pitfalls/confidential-data.qmd) before
  doing anything else.
- **Not a substitute for your judgment as an economist.** Claude can write
  the code; it cannot identify your effect, defend your specification, or
  decide whether your design is credible. See
  [what you must still do](pitfalls/judgment.qmd).

## Suggested reading order

If you have **30 minutes**, read:

1. [What is agentic coding?](big-picture/what-is-agentic.qmd)
2. [Install Claude Code](getting-started/install.qmd)
3. [LaTeX paper editing](examples/latex-paper.qmd) *or*
   [Replication package audit](examples/replication-package.qmd)

If you have **a free afternoon**, add:

4. [Plan mode, todos, slash commands](getting-started/plan-mode-and-todo.qmd)
5. The example page for your language: Stata, R, Python, Matlab, or Julia.
6. [How to ask](workflow/how-to-ask.qmd) and
   [Verifying output](workflow/verifying.qmd).

## A note on what's "fleshed out" right now

This site is a living draft. The two long-form examples (LaTeX paper editing
and replication-package audit) and the install guide are the most complete.
Other pages are short outlines that I'll fill in as colleagues use them and
tell me what's missing. If you find a section that would help you and
isn't there yet, **tell me** — that's the fastest way to make this useful.
